cues.text: Symphony runs in two ways.
Kubernetes: k3s on one VM, or kind for evaluation.
cues.say: Kubernetes: K 3 S on one V M, or kind for evaluation.

cues.text: There, each ticket gets its own pod.
Local mode: one process on the host, with no isolation.
Both use the same setup.

scenes.title: Redis, the API and a bootstrap token

cues.text: A new install starts with only Redis and the API.
cues.say: A new install starts with only Red-iss and the API.

cues.text: You apply the manifests. They make empty Secrets that setup fills later.
You fill one Secret yourself, with a bootstrap admin token.
Then you log in with that token, and run symphony setup.
In local mode, the process prints an admin token at its first start.
Until setup is complete, the other components wait.
The daemon keeps its heartbeat, and logs daemon setup incomplete once a minute at most.
Each merger idles, and logs merger not configured with what it lacks.
The assistant writes an idle heartbeat.
Health checks stay green, so Kubernetes does not restart them.
Jobs end with a setup incomplete event.
In a terminal, symphony setup starts the wizard.
It shows a progress bar, and does the GitHub App first.
A step that is done asks: Change it?
Secrets go into hidden prompts.
If the API refuses a value, you see why, and you can try again.
Scripts use one subcommand per step. Secrets come from standard input.
symphony setup --status prints the checklist.
cues.say: symphony setup, dash dash status, prints the checklist.

cues.text: Tern has the same flow in its Setup view.
Other people see a banner. For an admin, Setup opens by itself.
It shows the steps, the progress, and a card for the selected step.
Secret fields are masked.
A refused value is not saved, and the card says why.
A saved step shows what the API found.

scenes.title: Each one checks the real service

cues.text: Setup has seven steps. The API checks each value against the real service before it saves it.
Four steps are required.
Tracker: the Linear key and team, or the GitHub board and its status field.
GitHub App: it mints a token, lists the repositories, and reports missing permissions.
Repositories: the App must reach the default repository.
On Kubernetes, each repository also needs a running merger.
Models: each role needs a stored key or a host credential.
Three steps are optional.
Notifications send a test message first.
The assistant checks the Slack tokens, and the Discord message content intent.
Webhooks wait for one signed delivery from each source.
Setup is complete when every required step is done.

scenes.title: Write-only, and kept out of Redis

cues.text: Credentials are write-only. No response, log or audit entry contains them.
On Kubernetes, they go into named Secrets.
In local mode, they go to secrets.env in the root directory.
cues.say: In local mode, they go to secrets dot env in the root directory.

cues.text: Redis holds none of them.
Webhook secrets are the exception. Setup shows them once.
To get new ones, you rotate them.
On Kubernetes, a saved credential reaches the components through a restart.
The order is the daemon, each merger, the assistant, and the API last.
In local mode, a change applies at once.
SYMPHONY_PUBLIC_URL is the address where people and vendors reach the API.
cues.say: Symphony public URL is the address where people and vendors reach the API.

cues.text: Setup uses it for the webhook URLs. Without it, they use the address of the request.
When every required step is done, Symphony is ready.
Create your first ticket, and move it to an active state.
Follow it with symphony status, or in Tern.
The full guide is docs/install.md.
cues.say: The full guide is in the docs folder, in install dot M D.
